simple.meaning: כָּאָה (kâʼâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to despond ; causatively, to deject.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 4 times in Psalms, Ezekiel, Daniel, beginning at Psalms 10:10. The surrounding contexts include righteousness, covenant.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כָּאָה (H3512) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: כָּאָה (kâʼâh) / H3512 is traced through Psalms 10:10, Psalms 109:16, Ezekiel 13:22, Daniel 11:30 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H3512. ka 'ah [ כָּאָה ] verb Niph`al be disheartened, cowed (compare Arabic draw back timidly , abstain, through timidity ) — Niph`al Perfect וְנִכְאָה consecutive Dan 11:30 then shall he be cowed ; Participle לֵבָב נִכְאֵה Psa 109:16 downhearted (|| וְאֶבְיוֺן עָנִי ). Hiph`il Infinitive construct צַדִּיק לֵב הַכְאוֺת Ezek 13:22 ; but ᵑ7 ᵐ5 Co הכאבתן see כָּאַב .

occurrences.englishText: because he didn’t remember to show kindness,
Because with lies you have grieved the heart of the righteous, whom I have not made sad; and strengthened the hands of the wicked, that he should not return from his wicked way, and be saved alive.

For ships of Kittim will come against him. Therefore he will be grieved, and will return, and have indignation against the holy covenant, and will take action. He will even return, and have regard to those who forsake the holy covenant.
